T: It's been emotional. Pass the brown sauce.
D: Four friends lose a rigged card game and scramble to raise half a million pounds in a week.
P: Serve the mains when the lads plan the robbery over breakfast.
S: an East End seafood stall, without the jellied eels
Smoked mackerel flaked and blitzed with cream cheese, horseradish, lemon and black pepper, spread on toasted rye with sliced cucumber.
the rigged three-card brag game with Hatchet Harry

Peanuts coated in egg white, smoked paprika, brown sugar and chilli, roasted until glassy and crunchy, served in a bowl in the middle of the card table. Whisk 1 egg white until frothy. Toss with 400g raw peanuts, then with 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tbsp brown sugar, half a tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 160C for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring twice, until dry and crunchy. Cool on the tray and break up.

Pork rind dried overnight and roasted until puffed and crackling, then hit with malt vinegar and sea salt flakes, served warm in paper bags. Score 500g pork rind into strips, rub well with salt and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast on a rack at 220C for 30 minutes until puffed and crackling. Spray or brush lightly with 2 tbsp malt vinegar while hot, then toss in more sea salt flakes. Tip into paper bags.
M: Bacon, bangers, fried eggs, beans, mushrooms, blistered tomato and fried bread crisped in the bacon fat, brown sauce on the table. Grill 8 pork sausages for 15 minutes, turning. Fry 8 rashers bacon and keep warm, then fry 4 slices of bread in the bacon fat until crisp. Fry 250g mushrooms in butter and halve 4 tomatoes and grill until blistered. Warm a tin of baked beans. Fry 4 eggs. Load onto four warm plates and put brown sauce on the table.
the debt collector who brings his son along
Beef chuck braised in dark ale with onion and thyme for 2.5 hours, thickened, under a puff pastry lid, baked at 200C for 25 minutes. Thick chips and mushy peas with mint.
W: Self-raising flour, butter, sugar and currants mixed with milk, wrapped in a pudding basin under baking paper and foil, steamed 90 minutes, turned out with hot custard.
K: Two smoking barrels peated whisky sour
the two antique shotguns everyone is chasing

Smoky peated Scotch shaken with fresh lemon, honey syrup and egg white until silky, served over ice with a dash of bitters on the foam. Mix 2 tbsp honey with 2 tbsp warm water for honey syrup. For each drink, shake 50ml peated Scotch whisky, 25ml lemon juice, 15ml honey syrup and 1 egg white hard without ice, then with ice. Strain into a tumbler over ice and dot the foam with aromatic bitters.

s.note: an East End seafood stall, without the jellied eels
s.how: Flake 250g smoked mackerel, removing the skin and bones. Blitz with 150g cream cheese, 1 tbsp horseradish, lemon juice and black pepper until mostly smooth. Spread on toasted rye and top with thin cucumber slices.

Score 500g pork rind into strips, rub well with salt and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast on a rack at 220C for 30 minutes until puffed and crackling. Spray or brush lightly with 2 tbsp malt vinegar while hot, then toss in more sea salt flakes. Tip into paper bags.

m.note: the debt collector who brings his son along
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck with 2 onions and thyme, add 375ml ale and braise 2.5 hours. Thicken, pour into a dish, cover with puff and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Fry 1kg thick chips twice. Crush 300g cooked peas with butter and mint.

w.how: Rub 100g butter into 250g self-raising flour, stir in 75g sugar and 150g currants, then add 150ml milk to a soft dough. Press into a greased basin, cover with paper and foil and steam for 90 minutes. Turn out and serve with hot custard.
